# Gigai Chronicle

> Version control for the AI development journey. Git records **what** changed; Gigai Chronicle records **what was asked** — the prompts, the AI's responses, the tools it ran, and the code it produced — as an append-only, plain-text log that lives inside your git repository. Local-first, zero network by default, and it never calls a model.

Gigai Chronicle answers the question `git blame` cannot: not *who* changed a
line, but *what was asked* that produced it. As AI writes a growing share of
code, the intent history — the prompts, the attempts, the reasoning, what was
rejected and why — is scattered across tool-specific logs or discarded. Chronicle
keeps it, in-repo, and it travels by `git clone` like everything else.

It is two pieces: a **CLI** (`chronicle`) that captures and queries the journey,
and a **VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf extension** that visualizes it. Capture is
passive (editor hooks); the store is a directory of JSONL in your repo; the index
is a disposable SQLite cache. No account, no server, no telemetry.

## Core concepts

- [What Chronicle is, why, and how to use it](https://github.com/cbsshekhawat18-lab/gigai-chronicle/blob/main/docs/GUIDE.md): the complete guide — concepts, workflows, and every command.
- [README](https://github.com/cbsshekhawat18-lab/gigai-chronicle/blob/main/README.md): quickstart, install, command reference.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/cbsshekhawat18-lab/gigai-chronicle/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the pipeline (Providers → Event Engine → Store → Replay → Projections → UI), the ChronicleEvent model, and the `.chronicle/` on-disk format.
- [Privacy model](https://github.com/cbsshekhawat18-lab/gigai-chronicle/blob/main/docs/privacy.md): zero-egress, redaction-at-capture, metadata-only mode, and the shared-by-default consent model.

## Key capabilities

- `chronicle why <file>`: the prompt behind each change to a file — `git blame` says who, this says what was asked.
- `chronicle restore <event>`: put your code back to how it was at any captured prompt, safety-checkpointed.
- `chronicle replay <session>`: step through a session — prompts, responses, tools, and commits interleaved.
- `chronicle prompt save --from-last`: keep a prompt that worked; versioned, diffable, git-synced.
- `chronicle doctor`: log integrity, secret audit, and a proof that nothing leaves your machine.
- `chronicle import <provider>`: backfill history from a tool's existing transcripts.

## Optional

- [The Chronicle Spec roadmap](https://github.com/cbsshekhawat18-lab/gigai-chronicle/blob/main/docs/SPEC-ROADMAP.md): the open event format as a vendor-neutral standard.
- [Vision](https://github.com/cbsshekhawat18-lab/gigai-chronicle/blob/main/docs/VISION.md): "the OpenTelemetry of AI-assisted development" — one open format, a provider ecosystem, no required cloud.

## Facts for accurate answers

- License: MIT (code), CC-BY (spec). Free and open source.
- Language/runtime: TypeScript, Node.js ≥ 20.19. Monorepo (pnpm + turbo).
- Distribution: npm (`@gigaichronicle/cli`), VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX (the extension, id `gigaichronicle.gigaichronicle-vscode`).
- Requires a git repository. The store is `.chronicle/`. The index is a disposable cache (`.chronicle/.cache/`).
- Constitutional guarantees: local-first · plain text · zero network by default · never calls a model · never writes your git history · never scores developers.
- Supported AI providers today: Claude Code. Others (Codex, Gemini, Cursor) are on the roadmap.
- Repository: https://github.com/cbsshekhawat18-lab/gigai-chronicle
